latin: Propositio est per se cum uel subiectum diffinit praedicatum, uel praedicatum subiectum, uel ambo diffiniuntur per idem tertium.
translation: A proposition holds per se whenever the subject supplies the definition of the predicate, or the predicate that of the subject, or else a single third term defines them both.
